entries.file: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/Friendship Dynamics- Modelling Social Relationships through a Fuzzy Agent-Based Simulation.md
entries.source_access: Full 19-page article copy readable at https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/2c3b/ef77179d5fdaf4faddee8a632af966cd3ab8.pdf; publisher record at https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2011/765640.
resolved_initial_findings: The RQs no longer say friendship dissolves. The note explicitly says the relationship follows dF/dt = gF(1-F/K), with g=R_similarity×J and J=J0 exp(p×R_similarity), and ties cannot weaken or break (Section 5.2, Eqs. 5.1–5.3, printed pp. 12–13; primary PDF pp. 11–12).
Figure 4 example K=1 and F0=.01 and Figure 5 p=5.8, J0=.001 are accurately identified as illustrations; source says p and J0 were obtained experimentally (printed p. 13).

Four crisp/fuzzy similarity/friendship variants and two configurations are named. The ANOVA comparison across fuzzification levels and p<.001 are supported by Section 6, Table 2 and discussion (printed pp. 16–17). The note correctly limits this to internal model comparison and reports the authors’ no-empirical-support caveat for the logistic assumption.

unresolved_or_new_findings.finding: The claim that MentatFuzzAll produced higher mean couple similarity than every other variant in both configurations hides a source-internal prose/table conflict. The prose says it ‘beats’ the other versions on RSimilarity and RFriendship in both configurations (Section 6, printed p. 17), but Table 2 reports random-friendship RSimilarity 0.77 for both MentatFuzzSim and MentatFuzzAll (PDF p. 16). The table also marks crisp-friendship values as ‘all couples are friends,’ so those are not an ordinary graded comparison. The note repeats the prose as an unqualified result and does not flag the conflicting table values.
unresolved_or_new_findings.correction_needed: Report the table values and explicitly flag the discrepancy with the prose, or qualify the prose claim as conflicting with Table 2. Keep the ANOVA statement distinct from the pairwise/model-level result.

entries.metadata_and_references: Title/DOI/date and corrected displayed author Juan Pavón are consistent with the publisher record; tags use underscores/no spaces. All 67 reference links exactly match the original captured array in order.

entries.source_access: Complete 7-page primary author preprint readable at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.6822; Cambridge record https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/network-science/article/abs/friendship-networks-and-social-status/18CD7D21D1A2852C27C74374BAF22432.
verified_fixes: Model separates symmetric reciprocated-edge function alpha(rank difference) from directional one-way-edge function beta(rank difference); no self-edges and a uniform rank prior are stated (PDF pp. 2–3, Eqs. 1–11).

The estimation summary correctly describes hidden ranks/alpha-beta maximum likelihood with EM iteration and MCMC approximation for the rank posterior; posterior-averaged inferred rank is the reported measure (PDF pp. 2–4 and 5–6).

The empirical scale/results are accurate: 84 AddHealth school networks covering over 90,000 students; minimum-violations rankings have about 98% of unreciprocated edges directed lower-to-higher; inferred rank correlates with grade and popularity, with status interpretation explicitly conjectural (PDF pp. 3–6).
